My go-to transcription tool for Mac, MacWhisper, has rolled out a major update today, adding real-time meeting transcription, significantly improved speaker identification, tighter integration with Apple Intelligence, and new transcription models. Here are the details.

MacWhisper integrates more deeply with Apple Intelligence

I've mentioned many times before how indispensable MacWhisper is for me, especially in my podcast production workflow.

MacWhisper is one of the earliest AI transcription tools built for Mac. Since independent developer Jordi Bruin launched it in 2023, it has been continuously improved, with ongoing support for new models, services, and workflows.

These include automatic meeting recording, speaker identification, watched folders, system-wide dictation, local and cloud AI models, as well as integrations with services like Notion, Zapier, Obsidian, and n8n.

MacWhisper today updated to version 15.2, introducing a new speaker identification feature powered by NVIDIA's Nemotron 3 Diarization model, which was announced just hours ago.

This also brings us to another major feature of this update: real-time meeting transcription.

This feature has been at the top of MacWhisper's public roadmap for some time, and it's now finally here, allowing users to instantly browse, search, copy, or send live transcripts during meetings as they happen.

On the transcription model front, MacWhisper 15.2 adds Alibaba's QWEN3-ASR transcription model, which supports 22 languages, and further strengthens integration with Apple Intelligence, Siri, Spotlight, and Shortcuts on macOS 27.

Users running macOS (including those in the European Union) can now search transcripts system-wide, open them with Siri, pull text into Shortcuts, and reference the currently displayed transcript in Siri or Apple Intelligence requests.

Finally, MacWhisper 15.2 adds a folders and subfolders feature to help organize transcript files and meeting notes, and supports dragging existing transcript files into folders via the sidebar.
